title: The Budget Just Raised Savings Tax to 24%… But Most Savers Still Pay £0 😱🏦 #shorts
description:
Tax on savings interest jumps to 24% next April (basic rate), but most savers still pay nothing.

What changed: Budget 2025 raised the tax rates on savings income by two points from 6 April 2027, and Budget 2026 (28 October) adds a further two points. So from 6 April 2027 the savings basic rate is 24% (now 20%), the higher rate 44% (now 40%) and the additional rate 49% (now 45%). The government says 84% of income tax payers will be unaffected.

Why most savers pay nothing: the Personal Savings Allowance stays at £1,000 of interest a year for basic-rate taxpayers and £500 for higher-rate taxpayers (nothing for additional rate), and the starting rate for savings stays at £5,000. The Budget says a basic-rate taxpayer would need over £25,000 in savings, on top of any ISA, before paying tax. At 4% interest, £25,000 earns £1,000 a year.

The catch: cross into the higher-rate band (over £50,270 in England, Wales and Northern Ireland) and the allowance halves to £500; the rest is taxed at 44% from April 2027. And your interest counts as income: on a £50,000 salary, £1,000 of interest takes your income to £51,000, over £50,270, so your allowance is £500 and from April 2027 you'd pay £220 on that interest.

Sources: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/budget-2026-document/budget-2026-html (section 3.9) · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/budget-2026-overview-of-tax-legislation-and-rates-ootlar/budget-2026-overview-of-tax-legislation-and-rates-ootlar · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/budget-2026-overview-of-tax-legislation-and-rates-ootlar/annex-a-rates-and-allowances · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/income-tax-personal-savings-allowance/income-tax-personal-savings-allowance · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/changes-to-tax-rates-for-property-savings-dividend-income/changes-to-tax-rates-for-property-savings-dividend-income

assumptions: Interest outside ISAs; employee, no other income; Personal Allowance £12,570 (income under £100,000).
England, Wales and NI bands: higher rate from £50,270. Savings rates are UK-wide; Scottish taxpayers' bands for the allowance differ.
Higher-rate example: £1,000 interest, allowance £500, £500 × 44% = £220 a year from 6 April 2027 (£200 at 40% in 2026-27).
Tip-over example: £50,000 salary + £1,000 interest = £51,000 > £50,270; allowance £500; tax £220 from April 2027.
Starting rate for savings (£5,000) only helps if other taxable income is low; it doesn't apply in these examples.
